answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake on a shared ledger before it can trade. A new agent starts on an island of limited trust, earning reputation only through verifiable work over time. Creating many fake identities is therefore not free: an attacker must fund every fake with its stake, like planting a cedar forest one costly tree at a time, and misbehavior forfeits that stake. Honest agents keep their deposit and gain access, while Sybils face a rising cost that exceeds any gain from voting, spamming, or draining rewards.
